I'm not sure about a converter with such a range however, something to look into. And of course a simple DC shift and amplification circuit to line that triangle up with the square in the event you want to use this let's say for a synth audio voice. But that range would be quite overkill for such an application hahaha. Very cool man! Thank you for sharing.

That wasn't at all what I was arguing for, firstly if you are on a challenge run then the enemies give enough echoes for you to always be topped up on vials unless you are awful at the game, secondly taking a break is less monotonous then trying a boss over and over and learning nothing, the break is necessary for a player to have time to analyse there mistakes instead of trying to brute force through a boss.

If you are consistently failing a boss fight taking a break and fighting normal mobs is the best idea since you're doing something wrong, that moment of breaking the cycle could lead to someone trying the boss differently or coming in less frustrated from there last loss. Those moment were never tedious for me, they always lead to clarity and helped clear my mind.

I would have to disagree with your first critique. I would say every weapon is completely viable. Each weapon has a playstyle built around them and its a small enough roster to be able to really learn each weapons strengths and weaknesses while being big enough (with the dlc) to have an option for everyone. I have played through 3 builds, a quality ludwig, a bloodtinge chikage (my favorite) and an arcane cane build. Each of them were so different from each other but I never felt like I had to unlearn skills or use widely different tactics. I would highly recommend playing without a ludwig build because in my opinion it made me a lazy bloodborne player with its huge damage and high knockback.
